item.title: CVE-2026-114516 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 9.8
item.description: Thursday 19 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 9.8 | Etherpad is a real-time collaborative editor. From 1.8.14 until 3.3.3, the pre-authentication /static/* plugin asset handler in src/node/utils/Minify.ts performs a backslash-to-forward-slash conversion after src/node/utils/sanitizePathname.ts has completed its POSIX path checks. On POSIX systems the sanitizer correctly treats backslashes as ordinary filename bytes, but the later conversion turns encoded backslash-separated parent-directory segments into traversal components without revalidation or containment. The expressPreSession registration and the always-present ep_etherpad-lite core pseudo-plugin make this path reachable without credentials, allowing a remote attacker to read any file available to the Etherpad process. Disclosed configuration or environment secrets can expose administrator credentials, after which the administrator plugin installer can provide in-process code execution and full server compromise. This issue is fixed in version 3.3.3.

item.title: CVE-2026-133430 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 5.4
item.description: Thursday 19 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 5.4 | A flaw was found in Keycloak. This vulnerability allows an authenticated remote attacker to cause a denial of service by terminating active sessions of arbitrary users. When processing Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML) documents that lack a root signature, Keycloak accepts the request as long as any assertion within the document is signed, without verifying its context or placement. An attacker holding a validly signed assertion can embed it into an unsigned logout request for another user, causing Keycloak to accept the forged request and terminate the victim's session.

item.title: CVE-2026-133476 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 8.8
item.description: Thursday 19 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 8.8 | In Dolibarr before 24.0.3, dolForgeSQLCriteriaCallback() in htdocs/core/lib/functions.lib.php allows account takeover because it strips only a single table-name prefix from a Universal Search Filter (sqlfilters) operand before checking it against the forbidden-field denylist (pass, pass_crypted, api_key). MariaDB and MySQL accept a two-level qualification such as schema.alias.column, so an operand of the form dolibarr.u.pass_crypted survives the check and is emitted into the WHERE clause. A remote authenticated user holding only the holiday read and readall permissions, which confer no user-management or administrative access, can use the resulting boolean oracle at GET /api/index.php/holidays to recover any user's bcrypt password hash and api_key one character at a time, including an administrator's. Because api_key is accepted directly by the REST API as a bearer credential, this yields full administrative control of the application. This bypasses the fix for CVE-2026-89012, which added only a strtolower() call and did not address prefix depth. The same denylist also omits pass_temp, which stores a password in cleartext, as well as national_registration_number, salary, birth, address, personal_mobile and note_private.

item.title: CVE-2026-61798 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 8.1
item.description: Thursday 19 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 8.1 | netty-incubator-codec-ohttp implements Oblivious HTTP (OHTTP) gateway and client functionality using Netty. Prior to 0.0.23.Final, BoringSSLAsymmetricCipherKeyPair.toString in codec-ohttp-hpke-classes-boringssl/src/main/java/io/netty/incubator/codec/hpke/boringssl/BoringSSLAsymmetricCipherKeyPair.java includes its private parameter, BoringSSLAsymmetricKeyParameter.toString in codec-ohttp-hpke-classes-boringssl/src/main/java/io/netty/incubator/codec/hpke/boringssl/BoringSSLAsymmetricKeyParameter.java renders the complete private-key byte array when isPrivate is true, and BoringSSL.EVP_HPKE_KEY_init_or_throw in codec-ohttp-hpke-classes-boringssl/src/main/java/io/netty/incubator/codec/hpke/boringssl/BoringSSL.java includes rejected privateKeyBytes in an exception message. Applications that log affected key-pair objects or initialization exceptions can persist complete HPKE private key material in logs or telemetry. Anyone who can read those records can recover the key and may compromise OHTTP message confidentiality or authenticity expectations while the key remains usable. This issue is fixed in version 0.0.23.Final.

item.title: CVE-2026-61799 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 5.3
item.description: Thursday 19 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 5.3 | netty-incubator-codec-ohttp implements Oblivious HTTP (OHTTP) gateway and client functionality using Netty. Prior to 0.0.23.Final, BinaryHttpParser in codec-bhttp/src/main/java/io/netty/incubator/codec/bhttp/BinaryHttpParser.java accumulates attacker-controlled Binary HTTP variable-length integers into the int offset sumBytes. BinaryHttpParser.readRequestHead, BinaryHttpParser.readFieldLine, and BinaryHttpParser.getIndeterminateLength can narrow long lengths into that offset, causing integer wraparound before buffer indices are calculated. A remote peer that supplies a valid large encoded length to BinaryHttpParser or BinaryHttpDecoder can trigger an unchecked bounds exception from a small malformed message, fail or close the channel, and repeatedly cause denial of service. Java and Netty bounds checks prevent memory corruption, and no information disclosure was observed. This issue is fixed in version 0.0.23.Final.

item.title: CVE-2026-61827 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 8.7
item.description: Thursday 19 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 8.7 | netty-incubator-codec-ohttp implements Oblivious HTTP (OHTTP) gateway and client functionality using Netty. item.title: CVE-2026-63124 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 7.5
item.description: Thursday 19 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 7.5 | netty-incubator-codec-ohttp implements Oblivious HTTP (OHTTP) gateway and client functionality using Netty. Prior to 0.0.23.Final, BinaryHttpParser.readFieldLine in codec-bhttp/src/main/java/io/netty/incubator/codec/bhttp/BinaryHttpParser.java treats a complete field line that ends exactly at a known field-section boundary as incomplete and returns without consuming bytes. BinaryHttpParser.readFieldSection then leaves fieldSectionLength unchanged and repeats the loop because its forward-progress checks are Java assertions, which are normally disabled in production. A remote peer that sends a known-length Binary HTTP header or trailer section ending at that boundary can make the parser spin indefinitely and pin the Netty event-loop or worker thread responsible for the channel. This issue is fixed in version 0.0.23.Final.

item.title: CVE-2026-63202 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 7.5
item.description: Thursday 19 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 7.5 | netty-incubator-codec-ohttp implements Oblivious HTTP (OHTTP) gateway and client functionality using Netty. Prior to 0.0.23.Final, BinaryHttpParser.readFieldSection in codec-bhttp/src/main/java/io/netty/incubator/codec/bhttp/BinaryHttpParser.java loops while fieldSectionLength is nonzero and relies on disabled-by-default assertions to require BinaryHttpParser.readFieldLine to return a value and consume bytes. A corrupt field line can consume more bytes than its understated declared section length and drive the counter negative, or a truncated field line can return without consuming data and leave the parser in the same state. An unauthenticated OHTTP peer can encrypt such Binary HTTP content under the gateway public configuration, reach OHttpRequestResponseContext.ContentDecoder.decodeChunk, and permanently pin a Netty event-loop thread at full CPU before application business logic. Multiple requests can exhaust the event-loop group and deny service until restart. This issue is fixed in version 0.0.23.Final.

item.title: CVE-2026-69133 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 5.3
item.description: Thursday 19 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 5.3 | netty-incubator-codec-ohttp implements Oblivious HTTP (OHTTP) gateway and client functionality using Netty. From 0.0.20.Final until 0.0.27.Final, OHttpClientCodec in codec-ohttp/src/main/java/io/netty/incubator/codec/ohttp/OHttpClientCodec.java and OHttpServerCodec in codec-ohttp/src/main/java/io/netty/incubator/codec/ohttp/OHttpServerCodec.java retain the consumed outer cumulationBuffer after a valid OHTTP exchange completes, even though OHttpRequestResponseContext.destroy in codec-ohttp/src/main/java/io/netty/incubator/codec/ohttp/OHttpRequestResponseContext.java releases the inner Binary HTTP cumulation and the channel remains active. A peer can complete a large request or response and leave the keep-alive connection idle, causing the client and server handlers to retain the current high-water pooled or direct buffer capacity until later inbound content replaces it or the handler is removed. Many long-lived idle connections can pin substantial memory and create availability pressure. The issue does not cause unbounded growth for repeated exchanges on a single channel. This issue is fixed in version 0.0.27.Final.

item.title: CVE-2026-77312 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 10.0
item.description: Thursday 19 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 10.0 | Flyto2 Core is an execution kernel for automation and AI-agent workflows. Prior to 2.26.8, the earlier CVE-2026-67429 remediation applied validate_path_with_env_config() to only a hand-picked set of file-writing modules, leaving data.csv.write in src/core/modules/atomic/data/csv_write.py, data.json_to_csv in src/core/modules/atomic/data/json_to_csv.py, file.copy in src/core/modules/atomic/file/copy.py, and file.move in src/core/modules/atomic/file/move.py outside the FLYTO_SANDBOX_DIR confinement boundary. The advisory also identifies unguarded modules across the broader data.*, file.*, and report-writer families. data.csv.write relies on a .. substring denylist that does not reject absolute paths, while the other named modules accept caller-controlled output or destination paths without the canonical guard. A caller able to execute modules or recipes can therefore write attacker-controlled content outside the configured sandbox, potentially overwriting application code, recipes, startup files, scheduled-task files, or authorization files and gaining code execution on the host. This issue is fixed in version 2.26.8.

item.title: CVE-2026-77313 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 7.1
item.description: Thursday 19 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 7.1 | Flyto2 Core is an execution kernel for automation and AI-agent workflows. Prior to 2.26.8, validate_url_ssrf in src/core/utils.py resolves and checks a hostname but returns the hostname URL rather than the validated address, and session.get in http.get performs an independent DNS lookup when connecting. A low-privileged caller with control of the hostname's DNS can make the first lookup return a public address and the connection-time lookup return an internal address, bypassing the SSRF guard for all modules that call it and exposing readable internal or metadata-service responses. Successful exploitation requires attacker-controlled DNS and a successful timing-dependent answer change between the two lookups. This issue is fixed in version 2.26.8.

item.title: CVE-2026-77314 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 6.3
item.description: Thursday 19 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 6.3 | Flyto2 Core is an execution kernel for automation and AI-agent workflows. Prior to 2.26.8, the MCP run_recipe tool in src/core/mcp_handler.py accepts a caller-controlled recipe_name that load_recipe() in src/cli/recipe.py appends to the src/recipes path without resolved-path containment. Parent-directory segments can therefore make Flyto load and execute a YAML workflow outside the bundled recipe directory, bypassing the boundary represented by list_recipes(). This does not necessarily provide unrestricted code execution because available workflow modules remain subject to Flyto's module policy, but it permits unintended execution of allowed browser, network, file, and data-processing modules. This issue is fixed in version 2.26.8.

item.title: CVE-2026-77315 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 8.5
item.description: Thursday 19 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 8.5 | Flyto2 Core is an execution kernel for automation and AI-agent workflows. item.title: CVE-2026-77316 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 7.1
item.description: Thursday 19 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 7.1 | Flyto2 Core is an execution kernel for automation and AI-agent workflows. Prior to 2.26.8, validate_url_ssrf() in src/core/utils.py validates one DNS answer and then returns the hostname, while guarded_aiohttp_request(), enforce_outbound_url(), and validate_url_with_env_config() allow the outbound connection to perform an independent second lookup. A caller with control of the hostname's DNS can make validation see a public address and make the connection see an internal address, bypassing the guard across its outbound consumers and exposing readable internal or metadata-service responses. The attack requires low or zero DNS TTL behavior and a successful timing-dependent answer change; static multiple-address answers are checked and do not provide the same bypass. This issue is fixed in version 2.26.8.

item.title: CVE-2026-133435 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 3.7
item.description: Thursday 19 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 3.7 | A flaw was found in Keycloak. When configured with a database that uses case-insensitive collation, Keycloak resolves realm URLs regardless of letter casing. A remote attacker can exploit this behavior by sending requests with alternate letter casing to bypass upstream reverse proxy access controls that rely on case-sensitive path matching. This issue can expose restricted authentication endpoints intended only for internal access, though Keycloak's internal authentication mechanisms remain intact.
